question: Any patient aged over 60 years, or with a history of peptic ulcer disease, taking a non-selective NSAID for joint pain should routinely receive co-prescription of a proton-pump inhibitor (PPI) for gastroprotection.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. NSAIDs inhibit COX-1-mediated prostaglandin synthesis in the gastric mucosa, impairing the protective mucus-bicarbonate barrier. Patients aged >60 or with peptic ulcer disease have significantly elevated GI bleeding risk and must receive a PPI whenever an NSAID is prescribed.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. NICE guidelines and standard prescribing practice mandate PPI co-prescription with NSAIDs in high-risk groups: age >60, history of peptic ulcer disease, concomitant corticosteroid or anticoagulant use, or high-dose/long-duration NSAID therapy. Omitting the PPI is the most common NSAID prescribing error in orthopaedic practice.
